title: Machine learning selected nucleoside derivatives for hydrogel testing
summary: A machine-learning model trained on 71 previously reported nucleoside derivatives was applied to an external set, from which the authors selected 24 candidates for hydrogel testing. They report gel formation for 20 of the 24 tested molecules and characterize cation-independent hydrogel behavior for 8-aminoguanosine and 8-hydroxyguanosine. A 2023 Sichuan University patent by the same team had already disclosed the model, 12 selected candidates and 10 gelation positives, including these two derivatives. This entry represents one study/campaign and does not claim that the 2024 article was the first public disclosure or that the compounds were novel.
ai_technology: Machine-learning classifier using molecular descriptors to predict nucleoside derivative hydrogel formation

source_review.scope: Primary Nature article page and PubMed Central indexed full text for model selection and experimental outcomes; PubMed record for date and affiliations; published patent application text for same-team prior disclosure and overlapping candidates.

evidence.tested: The paper reports that 20 of 24 externally selected nucleoside derivatives formed hydrogels in experimental validation. It also reports cation-independent hydrogel behavior for 8-aminoguanosine and 8-hydroxyguanosine.
evidence.unknown: A 2023 patent application from the same university/team already disclosed the same model, 12 selected derivatives, 10 gelation positives, and included 8-AG and 8-OHG. Do not treat the overlapping paper and patent as independent discoveries or claim first disclosure/compound novelty. Hydrogel behavior does not establish clinical benefit.
evidence.ai_role: The ML model predicted gel-forming ability and selected nucleoside derivatives for external experimental validation.
